author: fieldmap
note: op998 is delivery-proven and its FUNCTION has never been measured - which are different claims, as op13488 showed by computing ~a & b under a name meaning ~(a & ~b). Every operand pair here is exactly representable in f32, so the prediction is exact rather than approximate, and the four sums are all distinct from both their addends: a form returning either operand unchanged is visible.

author: fieldmap
note: op3290 fmul, same discipline. Case 2 has a negative operand and case 3 a product smaller than one of its factors, so neither an add nor a pass-through fits the four.

author: fieldmap
note: op2190 ffma, three sources: a*b + c. Three sources is where 'it returned something plausible' stops being an answer - two of the three can keep the witness's registers and the sum still looks like arithmetic. Case 3 is 0.5*0.5+0.25 = 0.5, which equals its own third operand, so it is the case that would hide a dropped multiply; the other three do not, and all four must hold.

author: fieldmap
note: op10826 madd, the integer three-source: a*b + c. Distinct answers for every case, and none equals any of its operands.

author: fieldmap
note: op11372, the comparison that yields a VALUE. NO EXPECT: the condition code is operand 2 and this record does not write it, so which relation the witness carries is what the four cases measure - three orderings, and exactly one relation is consistent with all of them. That is the same method that read op11375's condition code as greater-than, applied to the opcode g17cc actually uses for icmp.
function: (a == b) ? 1 : 0 - the witness's condition code is EQUALITY, and the four cases cover all three orderings: 10<20 and 20>10 both return 0, 10==10 and 5==5 both return 1. Exactly one relation fits all four.
